title: 0  Armed forces (Level 1)
rationale: The occupation involves significant physical, tactical, and real-time decision-making tasks that occur in unpredictable, non-digital environments. While AI is increasingly used for logistics, surveillance, and strategic planning, the core functions of military personnel remain fundamentally tied to physical presence and human judgment.

title: 01 Commissioned armed forces officers (Level 2)
rationale: Commissioned officers perform a mix of high-level strategic planning, which is increasingly supported by AI-driven data analysis, and critical real-time leadership in unpredictable physical environments. While AI can assist with logistics and intelligence processing, the core requirements of command, ethical judgment, and physical presence in the field remain fundamentally human-centric.

title: Occupational groups total
rationale: This represents the entire Finnish labor market, which encompasses a vast spectrum of roles ranging from highly automatable digital tasks to manual, physical labor. Because it is an aggregate of all occupations, the exposure score reflects the weighted average of both high-exposure knowledge work and low-exposure physical or interpersonal service roles.

title: 011 Commissioned armed forces officers (Level 3)
rationale: While commissioned officers perform significant administrative, strategic, and analytical knowledge work that is susceptible to AI-driven decision support, the core of the profession remains rooted in physical command, real-time human leadership, and unpredictable field operations. The necessity for human accountability and physical presence in high-stakes environments creates a significant barrier to full automation.

title: 0110 Commissioned armed forces officers (Level 4)

AI may assist with planning, logistics, intelligence analysis, and administrative paperwork, but these are peripheral to the core leadership and operational duties.

title: 0110. Commissioned armed forces officers (Level 5)

title: 0210 Non-commissioned armed forces officers (Level 4)

AI tools are already capable of automating query generation, performance tuning, and database maintenance, leading to significant restructuring of the role.

title: 2523 Computer network professionals (Level 4)
rationale: Computer network professionals design, configure, monitor, and troubleshoot networks, work that is almost entirely digital and done through software, configuration files, and command-line tools. AI is rapidly improving at scripting, configuration generation, log analysis, and incident diagnosis, so core tasks are highly exposed, though physical hardware installation and on-site troubleshooting provide some natural limits.

title: 2522. Systems administrators (Level 5)
rationale: Systems administration is a highly digital role centered on managing infrastructure, scripting, and troubleshooting, all of which are increasingly automated by AI-driven monitoring and self-healing systems. While human oversight remains necessary for complex architectural decisions and security strategy, the core tasks of the profession are being rapidly transformed by AI integration.

title: 2523. Computer network professionals (Level 5)
rationale: Computer network professionals perform work that is almost entirely digital, involving the design, maintenance, and troubleshooting of systems that are increasingly managed by AI-driven automation and software-defined networking. While high-level architecture and complex problem-solving require human judgment, the core tasks of monitoring, configuration, and security analysis are highly susceptible to AI-assisted optimization and automation.

title: 2529 Database and network professionals not elsewhere classified (Level 4)
rationale: Database and network professionals work almost entirely on computers, designing, configuring, monitoring, and troubleshooting systems through digital tools and code-like scripts, all domains where AI is advancing rapidly. AI already automates much of monitoring, query optimization, and routine configuration, and can generate scripts and diagnose faults, though physical hardware maintenance and on-site incident handling retain some human necessity.

title: 26 Legal, social and cultural professionals (Level 2)
rationale: This category encompasses a broad range of knowledge-intensive roles such as lawyers, social workers, and cultural professionals, which are primarily digital or information-based. While roles involving complex human empathy and legal judgment require human oversight, AI is rapidly automating document drafting, research, and analytical tasks, leading to significant restructuring of these professions.

title: 261 Legal professionals (Level 3)
rationale: Legal professionals perform knowledge-intensive work that is primarily digital, involving extensive document review, research, and drafting. AI tools are rapidly automating these core tasks, significantly increasing productivity and restructuring the traditional workflow of legal analysis.

title: 2529. Database and network professionals not elsewhere classified (Level 5)
rationale: This role is almost entirely digital, focusing on the configuration, maintenance, and optimization of network and database systems. Because these tasks involve structured data, code-based management, and logical problem-solving, they are highly susceptible to automation through AI-driven infrastructure management and predictive maintenance tools.

title: 2611 Lawyers (Level 4)
rationale: Lawyers' core work of legal research, drafting contracts and pleadings, analyzing case law, and advising clients is overwhelmingly text-based and performed on a computer, areas where AI language models are advancing rapidly. Remaining barriers include court appearances, client negotiation, professional accountability, and trust-based relationships, which keep the score below the maximum.

title: 2611. Lawyers (Level 5)
rationale: Legal work is highly document-intensive, involving extensive research, drafting, and analysis of digital information, all of which are core strengths of current AI models. While human judgment and courtroom presence remain essential, the core tasks of legal discovery and document preparation are undergoing rapid automation and restructuring.

title: 2612 Judges (Level 4)
rationale: Judges work predominantly with written materials, legal texts, and evidence analysis, which are information-processing tasks AI can increasingly support through legal research, drafting, and summarization. However, the core role requires courtroom presence, assessing witness credibility, weighing human factors, and bearing personal legal responsibility, which keep AI's direct replacement potential limited.

title: 2612. Judges (Level 5)
rationale: Judges perform high-level knowledge work involving complex legal analysis, document review, and decision-making, which are increasingly supported by AI tools for research and summarization. However, the role requires significant human judgment, ethical accountability, and in-person courtroom presence, which act as substantial barriers to full automation.

title: 2619. Legal professionals not elsewhere classified (Level 5)
rationale: This role involves high-level knowledge work, including legal research, document drafting, and complex analysis, all of which are primary domains for AI advancement. Because the work is almost entirely digital and relies on processing large volumes of information, AI tools are poised to significantly restructure core tasks and increase productivity.

title: 2619 Legal professionals not elsewhere classified (Level 4)
rationale: Legal professionals in this category work almost entirely with documents, research, legal analysis, and written advice, all of which are digital, text-based tasks where AI capabilities are advancing rapidly. Core activities such as drafting contracts, reviewing case law, and summarizing regulations are highly automatable, though client interaction, courtroom or negotiation work, and professional accountability keep some human judgment essential.

title: 262 Librarians, archivists and curators (Level 3)
rationale: Librarians and archivists perform significant knowledge work involving information management, cataloging, and research, which are increasingly automated by AI-driven search and classification tools. However, the role retains a strong interpersonal and physical component related to community engagement, physical collection management, and specialized human-led curation that limits full automation.

title: 2621 Archivists and curators (Level 4)
rationale: Archivists and curators work largely with information: cataloguing, describing, researching, and digitizing records and collections, all tasks where AI is improving rapidly (metadata generation, transcription, search, and retrieval). However, a substantial share of the work involves handling physical objects, conservation, on-site exhibition design, and direct engagement with donors, researchers, and the public, which limits full automation.

title: 26211 Archivists (Level 5)
rationale: Archivists perform predominantly digital knowledge work involving the classification, digitization, and retrieval of information, which are core domains for AI advancement. Large language models and automated metadata tagging are already capable of restructuring how archival tasks are performed, significantly increasing efficiency and reducing the need for manual processing.

title: 2622 Librarians and related information professionals (Level 4)
rationale: Librarians work largely with information retrieval, cataloguing, reference questions, and digital resources, all of which are highly amenable to AI language and search tools. However, the role also involves in-person patron assistance, teaching information literacy, community programming, and physical collection management, which provide some natural barriers to full automation.

title: 263 Social and religious professionals (Level 3)
rationale: This occupation involves a significant amount of knowledge work, such as research, counseling, and administrative tasks, which are increasingly susceptible to AI assistance. However, the core of the role relies heavily on human empathy, complex interpersonal relationships, and community presence, which remain difficult for AI to replicate.

title: 2631 Economists (Level 4)
rationale: Economists work almost entirely with information: building econometric models, analyzing data, writing reports, and communicating findings, all of which are digital tasks where AI is advancing rapidly. Core activities like data processing, forecasting, and literature synthesis are highly automatable, while remaining human value lies in judgment, policy advising, and stakeholder communication.

title: 26212 Curators (Level 5)
rationale: Curatorial work involves a significant amount of digital knowledge work, including research, documentation, and communication, which are highly susceptible to AI-assisted synthesis and organization. However, the role also requires physical interaction with collections, exhibition design, and human-centric stakeholder management, which provides a natural barrier to full automation.

title: 2622. Librarians and related information professionals (Level 5)
rationale: Librarians perform significant knowledge work involving information organization, research, and digital database management, which are highly susceptible to AI-driven automation. While the role retains a human-centric component for community engagement and physical collection management, the core information-processing tasks are increasingly being augmented or replaced by AI search and classification tools.

title: 2632 Sociologists, anthropologists and related professionals (Level 4)
rationale: Sociologists and anthropologists work predominantly with knowledge tasks such as literature review, qualitative data coding, survey and statistical analysis, and writing reports, all of which are digital and within AI's rapidly improving capabilities. Fieldwork, interviews, and ethnographic observation require human presence and trust, which provides a meaningful but partial barrier to AI exposure.

title: 2632. Sociologists, anthropologists and related professionals (Level 5)
rationale: This occupation is primarily knowledge-based, involving extensive data analysis, report writing, and literature review, all of which are highly susceptible to AI-driven automation. While the role requires human judgment for qualitative research and fieldwork, the core analytical and synthesis tasks are increasingly being augmented or performed by AI tools.

title: 2633 Philosophers, historians and political scientists (Level 4)
rationale: This occupation is predominantly knowledge work centered on reading, researching, analyzing texts, and writing, all of which are digital and in domains where AI language models are advancing rapidly. Human judgment, original interpretation, teaching, and some archival or fieldwork with physical sources keep it from the very highest end of the scale.

title: 2631. Economists (Level 5)
rationale: Economists perform knowledge-intensive work primarily on computers, involving data analysis, forecasting, and report writing, all of which are core domains for generative AI and machine learning. While high-level strategic interpretation remains human-centric, the automation of data processing and modeling significantly restructures the occupation.

title: 2633. Philosophers, historians and political scientists (Level 5)
rationale: This occupation is primarily knowledge-based, involving extensive research, writing, and analytical synthesis, all of which are domains where AI models are increasingly capable. While human judgment and original philosophical or historical interpretation remain critical, AI tools significantly accelerate the processing of large datasets and the drafting of academic or analytical content.

title: 2634 Psychologists (Level 4)
rationale: Psychologists do substantial knowledge work such as assessment, report writing, case documentation, and research analysis, all of which AI can meaningfully assist or partly automate. However, the core of the job involves therapeutic relationships, real-time human interaction, empathy, and ethical responsibility, which limit how much AI can replace the practitioner directly.

title: 2634. Psychologists (Level 5)
rationale: Psychology involves high-level interpersonal interaction, empathy, and complex human judgment that are difficult for AI to replicate. While AI can assist with administrative tasks, documentation, and providing supplementary therapeutic resources, the core of the profession relies on the physical presence and nuanced human connection essential for clinical practice.

title: 2635 Social work and counselling professionals (Level 4)
rationale: Social work and counselling centre on face-to-face, emotionally sensitive client relationships, home visits, crisis response, and trust-building, which AI cannot substitute for. AI can meaningfully assist with the documentation, case notes, report writing, referral information, and administrative parts of the role, so exposure is moderate rather than low.

title: 2635. (Not more specifically classified) Social work and counselling professionals (Level 5)
rationale: Social work and counseling rely heavily on human empathy, complex interpersonal relationships, and ethical judgment in unpredictable, real-world environments, which limits AI's ability to replace the core role. However, AI can significantly assist with the substantial administrative burden, documentation, and information synthesis required in the profession, leading to moderate exposure.

title: 26351 Social workers, etc. (Level 5)
rationale: Social work involves significant interpersonal interaction, emotional intelligence, and complex case management that requires human presence and ethical judgment. While AI can assist with administrative tasks, documentation, and data analysis, the core of the profession relies on human-to-human connection and physical intervention in unpredictable environments.

title: 2636 Religious professionals (Level 4)
rationale: Religious professionals such as priests and pastors work largely through in-person pastoral care, rituals, sermons delivered to live congregations, and personal counseling, all of which require human presence, trust, and spiritual authority. AI can assist with peripheral tasks like writing sermon drafts, administrative work, research, and scheduling, but the core relational and ceremonial functions remain difficult to automate.

title: 26352 Social planners, etc. (Level 5)
rationale: Social planners perform knowledge-intensive work involving data analysis, report writing, and policy development, all of which are highly susceptible to AI-driven automation and augmentation. While the role requires human judgment and stakeholder engagement, the core tasks of synthesizing information and drafting planning documents are increasingly being transformed by generative AI tools.

title: 2636. Religious professionals (Level 5)
rationale: Religious professionals rely heavily on interpersonal connection, emotional intelligence, and physical presence for rituals and community support, which are difficult for AI to replicate. While AI can assist with administrative tasks, sermon preparation, or theological research, the core of the role remains rooted in human-to-human interaction.

title: 264 Authors, journalists and linguists (Level 3)
rationale: The core tasks of this occupation—writing, editing, translating, and content creation—are entirely digital and represent the primary domains where generative AI excels. These roles face significant restructuring as AI tools can now draft, summarize, and translate text with high proficiency, fundamentally altering the nature of the work.

title: 2641 Authors and related writers (Level 4)
rationale: Authors and related writers perform almost entirely digital knowledge work: drafting, editing, researching, and revising text, all domains where AI language models are advancing rapidly. Core creative and narrative tasks are increasingly within AI capability, though human originality, reputation, audience relationships, and the physical-free but personally driven nature of the work provide some residual barrier.

title: 2641. Authors and related writers (Level 5)
rationale: Authors and writers perform work that is almost entirely digital and centered on content generation, a domain where generative AI is rapidly advancing. AI tools can already assist with drafting, editing, and research, leading to a fundamental restructuring of the creative writing process.

title: 2642. (Not more specifically classified) Journalists (Level 5)
rationale: Journalism is a predominantly digital profession involving research, writing, and content synthesis, all of which are core domains for generative AI. While human judgment, investigative ethics, and on-the-ground reporting remain essential, the automation of drafting, summarizing, and data analysis significantly restructures the traditional workflow.

title: 2642 Journalists (Level 4)
rationale: Journalists' core work is researching, writing, editing, and analyzing information, which is almost entirely digital and in domains where AI language models are advancing rapidly. Human judgment, source relationships, on-site reporting, and accountability still provide some barrier, keeping the score below the very highest levels.

title: 26422 Journalists (Level 5)
rationale: Journalism is a digital-first profession involving research, writing, and content synthesis, all of which are core domains for generative AI. While human judgment, investigative ethics, and physical presence for reporting remain valuable, the rapid automation of drafting, summarizing, and data analysis significantly restructures the traditional workflow.

title: 26423 Radio and television journalists (Level 5)
rationale: Journalism is a digital-first profession involving research, writing, and content synthesis, all of which are core domains for generative AI. While human judgment, investigative ethics, and on-the-ground reporting remain critical, the production and editing workflows are undergoing rapid automation and restructuring.

title: 2643. Translators, interpreters and other linguists (Level 5)
rationale: Translation and linguistic work are almost entirely digital and represent a primary domain where Large Language Models have demonstrated high proficiency. The core tasks of text processing, syntax analysis, and cross-lingual communication are being rapidly automated, leading to a fundamental restructuring of the profession.

title: 26421 Managing editors and subeditors (Level 5)
rationale: The work of managing editors and subeditors is almost entirely digital, involving text analysis, editing, and content management, all of which are core domains for generative AI. AI tools can already automate significant portions of copyediting, fact-checking, and structural refinement, leading to a major restructuring of the role.

title: 2643 Translators, interpreters and other linguists (Level 4)
rationale: Translation, interpreting and linguistic work is almost entirely performed on a computer or through spoken communication in digital channels, and machine translation and large language models already perform much of the core text-based work at high quality. Remaining human value lies in certified legal or medical translation, live interpreting in sensitive settings, cultural nuance, and accountability, which limits but does not prevent major restructuring of the occupation.

title: 265 Creative and performing artists (Level 3)
rationale: While creative and performing arts rely heavily on human expression, emotion, and physical presence, the industry is increasingly utilizing generative AI for ideation, drafting, and production. The core of the work remains human-centric, but the tools used for creation are undergoing a significant shift that will reshape workflows and productivity.

title: 265.. (Not more specifically classified) Creative and performing artists (Level 5)
rationale: Creative and performing artists engage in high-level knowledge work that is increasingly impacted by generative AI tools capable of producing text, imagery, and audio. While the core of artistic expression often relies on human intent and physical performance, the production process is becoming heavily digitized and susceptible to AI-driven augmentation and automation.

title: 265.  (Not more specifically classified) Creative and performing artists (Level 4)
rationale: This ISCO-08 subgroup covers creative and performing artists such as painters, sculptors, musicians, actors, dancers and writers, whose work is partly digital (composition, design, writing, visual art) and therefore highly susceptible to generative AI tools. However, much of the work involves live performance, physical embodiment, and personal artistic judgment that AI cannot replicate, which moderates the exposure.

title: 2651 Visual artists (Level 4)
rationale: Visual artists produce digital and physical work, and much of the creative process (concept sketches, digital illustration, design iterations, image generation) is increasingly done on computers where generative AI is advancing rapidly. However, original artistic vision, physical media work such as painting, sculpture and installations, and client or audience interaction retain a meaningful human component that limits full automation.

title: 2651. Visual artists (Level 5)
rationale: Visual arts are increasingly impacted by generative AI models capable of creating high-quality imagery, illustrations, and design assets in seconds. While human creativity and intent remain central, the core production tasks are shifting toward AI-assisted workflows, significantly restructuring the traditional labor process for artists.

title: 2653. Dancers and choreographers (Level 5)
rationale: The work of dancers and choreographers is fundamentally physical, relying on human movement, artistic expression, and real-time performance. While AI can assist with peripheral tasks like music composition or movement visualization, it cannot replace the core requirement of physical presence and human artistry.

title: 2653 Dancers and choreographers (Level 4)
rationale: Dancers and choreographers perform physically embodied, real-time artistic work in front of live audiences, which AI cannot replicate. AI may assist choreographers with music generation, visualization, or documentation and marketing tasks, but the core creative and physical work remains human-centered.

title: 2652. Musicians, singers and composers (Level 5)
rationale: While music composition and production are increasingly supported by AI tools, the core of the profession relies on human performance, artistic expression, and live interaction. AI can assist in the creative process, but it cannot replace the unique human element and physical presence required for live musical performance and interpretation.

title: 2652 Musicians, singers and composers (Level 4)
rationale: Musicians, singers and composers do creative work that is partly digital, as composing, arranging and producing music can be done on computers, and AI music generation is advancing quickly. However, performance is largely live, physical and interpersonal, requiring real-time presence, embodied skill and audience connection, which limits how much AI can replace the core job.

title: 2654 Film, stage and related directors and producers (Level 4)
rationale: Directing and producing work is predominantly knowledge and creative work involving scripting, planning, budgeting, scheduling, and editing, much of which can be supported by AI tools for storyboarding, post-production, and administration. However, the core job depends heavily on on-set leadership, real-time collaboration with actors and crews, artistic judgment, and physical production presence, which limit full automation.

title: 2656 Announcers on radio, television and other media (Level 4)
rationale: Broadcast announcing is predominantly a communication-based knowledge job: scripting, reading news, hosting, and producing audio or video content are all digital work products that AI can increasingly generate and voice. However, live on-air presence, real-time interaction with guests and audiences, and editorial judgment keep it short of the fully digital ceiling, and AI voice and video synthesis is already reshaping the field.

title: 2654. Film, stage and related directors and producers (Level 5)
rationale: While the creative vision and leadership aspects of directing and producing require human judgment and interpersonal management, much of the pre-production, planning, and administrative work is increasingly digital. AI tools are already impacting tasks like script analysis, scheduling, budgeting, and visual pre-visualization, though the core artistic and collaborative human elements remain essential.

title: 2655. Actors (Level 5)
rationale: While acting requires unique human emotional expression and physical presence, the industry is experiencing high exposure due to AI-driven advancements in digital synthesis, voice cloning, and CGI. These technologies are increasingly automating background roles and post-production tasks, fundamentally reshaping the creative process and labor demand in the sector.

title: 2655 Actors (Level 4)
rationale: Acting is a performance-based creative job centered on physical presence, voice, emotional expression, and real-time interaction with directors, co-actors, and audiences, which provides a meaningful barrier to AI replacement. However, AI video generation, voice cloning, and digital likeness tools threaten background, voice-over, and commercial work, and script analysis and casting tasks are increasingly AI-assisted, so exposure is substantial.

title: 2656. Announcers on radio, television and other media (Level 5)
rationale: The occupation involves significant digital content creation, scriptwriting, and information synthesis, which are highly susceptible to AI-driven automation and augmentation. While the role requires human presence and personality for broadcasting, the underlying production tasks are increasingly being reshaped by AI tools for editing, voice synthesis, and content generation.

title: 3  Technicians and associate professionals (Level 1)
rationale: This is a broad category encompassing diverse technical roles that rely heavily on digital information processing, analysis, and documentation. While many of these roles require specific domain expertise and human judgment, the core tasks are increasingly susceptible to AI-driven automation and augmentation tools.

title: 311 Physical and engineering science technicians (Level 3)
rationale: This role involves a mix of technical knowledge work and physical site-based tasks, such as testing, monitoring, and data collection. While AI can significantly enhance the analysis and reporting aspects of the job, the requirement for physical presence and hands-on interaction with equipment provides a natural barrier to full automation.

title: 2659 Creative and performing artists not elsewhere classified (Level 4)
rationale: This ISCO 2659 group covers a mix of creative and performing work such as puppeteers, clowns, magicians, and other artists not classified elsewhere. Much of the core work is physical, live, and interpersonal (stage performance, audience interaction), which limits AI displacement, though AI tools can assist with scripting, design, and promotional or creative ideation.

title: 2659. Creative and performing artists not elsewhere classified (Level 5)
rationale: This occupation involves creative knowledge work that is increasingly influenced by generative AI tools for drafting, ideation, and content production. While human judgment, unique artistic vision, and physical performance remain essential, the core creative processes are highly susceptible to AI-driven augmentation and automation.

title: 31 Science and engineering associate professionals (Level 2)
rationale: This category involves technical knowledge work, data analysis, and documentation, which are highly susceptible to automation via AI tools. While these roles often require some physical oversight or field-based technical tasks, the core information-processing and analytical components are increasingly being augmented or replaced by AI systems.

title: 3111. Chemical and physical science technicians (Level 5)
rationale: This role involves a mix of physical laboratory work, sample preparation, and equipment maintenance, which are difficult to automate. However, the data analysis, documentation, and reporting components are increasingly susceptible to AI-driven automation and software integration.

title: 3112. (Not more specifically classified) Civil engineering technicians (Level 5)
rationale: Civil engineering technicians perform a mix of digital knowledge work, such as CAD drafting and technical documentation, and physical site inspections. While the digital components are highly susceptible to AI-driven design and analysis tools, the requirement for on-site verification and physical project coordination provides a significant buffer against full automation.

title: 3111 Chemical and physical science technicians (Level 4)
rationale: Chemical and physical science technicians split their time between hands-on laboratory work (preparing samples, operating instruments, maintaining equipment, running experiments) and digital tasks such as data recording, analysis, and reporting. AI and automation can meaningfully assist with the data processing, instrument control, and documentation parts, but the physical lab work and handling of materials keep a substantial share of the job requiring human presence.

title: 3112 Civil engineering technicians (Level 4)
rationale: Civil engineering technicians spend much of their time on digital work such as drafting, CAD modelling, calculations, and report preparation, which AI tools are already accelerating. However, a significant share of the role involves on-site surveying, inspection, and materials testing that require physical presence and human judgment, limiting full automation.

title: 31122 Civil engineering technicians (Level 5)
rationale: Civil engineering technicians perform a mix of office-based technical design, documentation, and data analysis, which are increasingly susceptible to AI-driven automation. However, the role also requires physical site visits, coordination with construction teams, and adherence to local safety regulations, which provide a necessary human-in-the-loop component.

title: 31123 Cartographic and surveying technicians (Level 5)
rationale: This role involves significant digital work, including processing spatial data, drafting maps, and utilizing GIS software, all of which are highly susceptible to AI automation. While some tasks require field-based surveying, the core analytical and drafting components are increasingly being streamlined by AI-driven image processing and automated mapping tools.

title: 3113. Electrical engineering technicians (Level 5)
rationale: Electrical engineering technicians perform a mix of technical knowledge work and hands-on physical tasks such as testing, installation, and maintenance. While AI can assist with documentation, circuit design, and diagnostic analysis, the core requirement for physical presence and manual interaction with hardware provides a significant barrier to full automation.

title: 3114. Electronics engineering technicians (Level 5)
rationale: Electronics engineering technicians perform a mix of digital knowledge work, such as circuit design and simulation, and physical tasks like testing and repairing hardware. While AI can significantly accelerate the design and diagnostic phases, the requirement for physical interaction with hardware and troubleshooting in real-world environments limits the total automation potential.

title: 3113 Electrical engineering technicians (Level 4)
rationale: Electrical engineering technicians split their time between desk-based work (circuit design support, drawings, documentation, test data analysis, troubleshooting procedures) that AI can increasingly assist with, and hands-on work such as installing, wiring, testing and repairing equipment on site that requires physical presence. AI will likely speed up the information-processing parts and change diagnostic workflows, but a substantial share of the job stays physical, so exposure is moderate.

title: 3114 Electronics engineering technicians (Level 4)
rationale: Electronics engineering technicians split their time between desk-based work (circuit design support, documentation, test data analysis, troubleshooting procedures) and hands-on tasks such as assembling, soldering, repairing and testing physical equipment in labs or the field. AI can meaningfully assist with the information-processing parts like diagnostics, schematics and reporting, but the hardware manipulation and on-site presence remain a substantial barrier.

title: 3115 Mechanical engineering technicians (Level 4)
rationale: Mechanical engineering technicians spend much of their time on digital work such as CAD drafting, technical documentation, calculations, simulation setup, and reporting, all of which AI tools are rapidly improving at. However, a substantial share of the role involves hands-on testing, inspecting, and assembling equipment on site or in workshops, which limits how far AI can reshape the job in the near term.

title: 3116 Chemical engineering technicians (Level 4)
rationale: Chemical engineering technicians split their time between computer-based work (data analysis, process monitoring, documentation, report writing, simulation support) and hands-on laboratory or plant tasks such as sampling, running equipment, and handling chemicals. AI can meaningfully assist with the information-processing parts, but the physical lab and plant work requires human presence and manual skill, placing the occupation in the moderate range.

title: 3117 Mining and metallurgical technicians (Level 4)
rationale: Mining and metallurgical technicians spend much of their time on physical, on-site work such as operating and maintaining plant equipment, sampling, and safety inspections in industrial environments, which limits AI's direct reach. However, a meaningful share of the role involves process monitoring, data analysis, laboratory results, and technical documentation, where AI tools can increasingly assist and speed up work.

title: 3115. Mechanical engineering technicians (Level 5)
rationale: Mechanical engineering technicians perform a mix of digital design, technical documentation, and physical testing or oversight. While AI tools are increasingly capable of automating CAD tasks and predictive maintenance analysis, the role requires physical interaction with machinery and real-world troubleshooting that limits full automation.

title: 3116. Chemical engineering technicians (Level 5)
rationale: Chemical engineering technicians perform a mix of laboratory analysis, data monitoring, and physical equipment maintenance. While AI can significantly enhance data processing and predictive maintenance tasks, the role requires physical presence for sample handling, equipment calibration, and safety oversight in industrial environments.

title: 3117. Mining and metallurgical technicians (Level 5)
rationale: This role involves a mix of technical knowledge work and physical site-based monitoring, which limits the extent of AI automation. While AI can assist with data analysis, predictive maintenance, and process optimization, the requirement for on-site physical inspection and operational oversight in metallurgical environments provides a significant barrier to full automation.

title: 3119 Physical and engineering science technicians not elsewhere classified (Level 4)
rationale: Technicians in physical and engineering sciences do a mix of hands-on laboratory, workshop, and equipment work alongside substantial data handling, measurement analysis, documentation, and reporting. AI can meaningfully assist with the information-processing parts such as data analysis, simulation, and report generation, but a significant share of the job still requires physical presence, instrument operation, and manual skill.

title: 3118 Draughtspersons (Level 4)
rationale: Draughtspersons (technical drawing and CAD work) produce fully digital work products such as engineering drawings, schematics, and 3D models created on a computer. AI tools for generative design, drafting automation, and CAD assistance are advancing rapidly, threatening much of the routine drafting work, though some coordination with engineers and site-related judgment remain.

title: 3118. Draughtspersons (Level 5)
rationale: Draughting is a highly digital profession centered on CAD software, which is increasingly being integrated with generative AI for automated design, 3D modeling, and error checking. Because the core output is digital and rule-based, AI tools are rapidly automating the most time-consuming aspects of technical drawing and documentation.

title: 3119. Physical and engineering science technicians not elsewhere classified (Level 5)
rationale: This role involves a mix of technical knowledge work and physical tasks, such as conducting laboratory tests or monitoring industrial processes. While AI can assist with data analysis and documentation, the requirement for physical presence, equipment operation, and real-world observation provides a significant buffer against full automation.

title: 312 Mining, manufacturing and construction supervisors (Level 3)
rationale: This role involves a blend of on-site physical supervision and digital administrative tasks like reporting, scheduling, and resource management. While AI can significantly optimize logistics, planning, and safety monitoring, the core requirement for physical presence and real-time human judgment in unpredictable industrial environments limits the overall exposure.

title: 31121 Building construction technicians (Level 5)
rationale: Building construction technicians perform a mix of office-based planning, documentation, and site-based supervision. While AI can assist with digital tasks like drafting, scheduling, and project management, the core requirement for physical site inspections and real-time coordination with construction crews limits the overall impact.

title: 3121 Mining supervisors (Level 4)
rationale: Mining supervisors direct underground and surface mining operations, which depend heavily on physical presence, safety inspections, and real-time coordination of crews in hazardous, unpredictable environments. AI can assist with peripheral tasks such as production reporting, scheduling, maintenance planning, and monitoring data, but the core supervisory and on-site work remains largely human-driven.

title: 3121. Mining supervisors (Level 5)
rationale: Mining supervisors perform a mix of on-site operational management, safety oversight, and physical coordination that requires human presence in unpredictable environments. While AI can assist with data analysis, predictive maintenance, and reporting, the core requirement of managing physical mining operations and personnel on-site limits the scope for full automation.

title: 3122. Manufacturing supervisors (Level 5)
rationale: Manufacturing supervisors balance physical oversight of production floors with digital tasks like scheduling, reporting, and resource management. While AI can optimize workflows and predictive maintenance, the core requirement for on-site human judgment, team management, and real-time physical problem-solving limits the extent of automation.

title: 3123 Construction supervisors (Level 4)
rationale: Construction supervisors spend most of their time on physical sites overseeing workers, equipment, safety, and real-time problem solving in unpredictable environments, which AI cannot directly perform. AI can assist with peripheral knowledge work such as scheduling, documentation, cost tracking, and drawing interpretation, but the core supervisory presence remains human-dependent.

title: 3122 Manufacturing supervisors (Level 4)
rationale: Manufacturing supervisors split their time between coordinating production, scheduling, reporting, and quality documentation, which AI can meaningfully assist with through planning tools, monitoring dashboards, and automated reporting. However, a substantial share of the role requires physical presence on the factory floor, hands-on problem solving with machinery, and direct leadership of workers, which limits AI's direct displacement of core duties.

title: 3123. Construction supervisors (Level 5)
rationale: Construction supervision involves a significant amount of on-site physical presence, coordination, and real-time problem-solving in unpredictable environments, which limits AI's ability to fully automate the role. However, AI can assist with administrative tasks like scheduling, project documentation, and progress monitoring, leading to moderate exposure.

title: 3131 Power production plant operators (Level 4)
rationale: Power production plant operators monitor and control generation equipment, much of which is physical and safety-critical, requiring on-site presence, manual inspection, and rapid response to equipment faults. AI and automated control systems already handle much of the monitoring and optimization, so AI may assist with diagnostics and reporting, but the core work of supervising physical plant operations remains largely human-dependent.

title: 3132. Incinerator and water treatment plant operators (Level 5)
rationale: The role involves monitoring and operating physical machinery and chemical processes in a plant environment, which requires significant physical presence and manual intervention. While AI can assist with predictive maintenance and data analysis of sensor inputs, the core tasks of equipment maintenance and physical plant management remain largely resistant to automation.

title: 313 Process control technicians (Level 3)
rationale: Process control technicians work in a digital-heavy environment monitoring and adjusting automated systems, making them highly susceptible to AI-driven predictive maintenance and autonomous optimization. While the role requires physical presence for equipment maintenance and emergency intervention, the core analytical and monitoring tasks are increasingly being handled by intelligent software.

title: 3131. Power production plant operators (Level 5)
rationale: While the role involves monitoring digital control systems and dashboards, which are increasingly AI-assisted, the occupation requires physical presence for maintenance, safety oversight, and emergency response in a hazardous industrial environment. The core responsibility of ensuring physical plant safety and operational integrity acts as a significant barrier to full automation.

title: 3132 Incinerator and water treatment plant operators (Level 4)
rationale: Incinerator and water treatment plant operators spend most of their time monitoring and physically operating industrial equipment, valves, pumps, and chemical dosing systems on-site, with safety-critical real-time responsibilities. AI may assist with process monitoring, anomaly detection, and documentation or reporting, but the core hands-on operational and physical presence work limits exposure.

title: 3134 Petroleum and natural gas refining plant operators (Level 4)
rationale: Refinery plant operators work primarily in industrial control rooms and on-site plant areas, monitoring and adjusting complex process equipment in real time under safety-critical conditions. AI can assist with process optimization, predictive maintenance alerts, and documentation, but the core work of physically inspecting equipment, responding to upsets, and operating valves and units requires human presence and manual intervention.

title: 3133 Chemical processing plant controllers (Level 4)
rationale: Chemical processing plant controllers monitor and adjust industrial process control systems, a role that is partly digital (reading dashboards, analyzing process data, documenting operations) and partly tied to physical plant presence, safety-critical field inspections, and hands-on intervention. AI can meaningfully assist with anomaly detection, predictive maintenance, and automated control optimization, but a substantial share of the job still requires on-site human judgment and responsibility for safety.

title: 3133. Chemical processing plant controllers (Level 5)
rationale: While the role involves monitoring digital control systems, it requires physical presence in a hazardous industrial environment to manage equipment and respond to real-time physical anomalies. AI can enhance predictive maintenance and process optimization, but the core responsibility of physical oversight and safety management remains human-centric.

title: 3134. Petroleum and natural gas refining plant operators (Level 5)
rationale: This role involves monitoring and controlling complex physical industrial processes, which requires significant physical presence and real-time safety oversight. While AI can assist in predictive maintenance and process optimization, the core tasks are tied to physical infrastructure and manual intervention in unpredictable environments.

title: 3135 Metal production process controllers (Level 4)
rationale: Metal production process controllers monitor and adjust industrial equipment in steel mills and foundries, which requires substantial physical presence on the plant floor and real-time response to hazardous conditions. AI can meaningfully assist with the data-heavy parts of the job, such as process monitoring, anomaly detection, and optimization of control parameters, but hands-on supervision and physical inspection remain central.

title: 3135. Metal production process controllers (Level 5)
rationale: This role involves monitoring and controlling physical industrial processes, which requires human oversight for safety and real-time physical intervention. While AI can optimize process parameters and predictive maintenance, the core task remains tied to the physical operation of machinery in a factory environment.

title: 314 Life science technicians and related associate professionals (Level 3)
rationale: This role involves a mix of laboratory-based physical experimentation and digital data analysis. While AI can significantly accelerate the analysis, reporting, and documentation phases of the work, the core requirement for manual laboratory procedures and physical sample handling provides a natural barrier to full automation.

title: 3139 Process control technicians not elsewhere classified (Level 4)
rationale: Process control technicians monitor and adjust industrial equipment and control systems, combining digital data interpretation (sensor readings, alarm logs, control software) with hands-on work on physical plant equipment. AI can assist substantially with monitoring, anomaly detection, and documentation, but a significant share of the job requires physical presence at industrial sites and manual intervention.

title: 3141 Life science technicians (excluding medical) (Level 4)
rationale: Life science technicians work largely in laboratories, setting up experiments, operating instruments, preparing samples and maintaining equipment, which requires significant hands-on physical presence. However, much of their work involves data recording, analysis, literature and protocol documentation, and interpreting results, which AI tools can increasingly support or automate, and AI-driven lab automation is also advancing.

title: 3139. Process control technicians not elsewhere classified (Level 5)
rationale: This role involves monitoring and controlling technical processes, which is increasingly digitized and supported by AI-driven predictive maintenance and automation systems. However, it still requires physical presence to oversee machinery, perform manual adjustments, and respond to unpredictable physical malfunctions that AI cannot yet resolve.

title: 3141. Life science technicians (excluding medical) (Level 5)
rationale: This role involves a mix of physical laboratory work, sample collection, and data analysis. While the data processing and reporting aspects are highly susceptible to AI automation, the physical requirements of conducting experiments and maintaining laboratory equipment provide a significant barrier to full automation.

title: 3142 Agricultural technicians (Level 4)
rationale: Agricultural technicians split their time between field work, livestock or crop handling, and machinery operation, which require physical presence and hands-on skill in unpredictable farm environments. The knowledge-work portions, such as record keeping, data analysis from sensors, crop monitoring reports, and advisory documentation, can be meaningfully assisted by AI tools. Overall this places the occupation in the moderate range.

title: 3142. Agricultural technicians (Level 5)
rationale: Agricultural technicians perform a mix of field-based physical monitoring and digital data analysis. While AI can enhance crop monitoring and yield prediction, the role requires significant physical presence and on-site decision-making that cannot be fully automated.

title: 3143. Forestry technicians (Level 5)
rationale: Forestry technicians perform a significant amount of field-based work, including surveying, monitoring, and managing forest operations, which requires physical presence and environmental judgment. While AI can assist with data analysis from remote sensing or drone imagery, the core of the job remains tied to physical site management and hands-on technical tasks that are difficult to automate.

title: 315 Ship and aircraft controllers and technicians (Level 3)
rationale: While this role involves significant digital monitoring and data analysis, it is constrained by high-stakes, real-time physical safety requirements and complex regulatory environments. AI will likely serve as a powerful decision-support tool for navigation and traffic management, but the necessity for human accountability and physical oversight in unpredictable environments limits full automation.

title: 3143 Forestry technicians (Level 4)
rationale: Forestry technicians split their time between field work (measuring stands, inspecting forests, supervising harvesting, planting and tending trees in varied outdoor conditions) and office work (data recording, planning, reporting, mapping with GIS software). AI can meaningfully assist the planning, mapping, remote sensing analysis and documentation parts, but the substantial on-site physical and supervisory component limits overall exposure.

title: 3151 Ships' engineers (Level 4)
rationale: Ships' engineers operate and maintain marine propulsion, power, and mechanical systems, which is largely hands-on work performed aboard vessels in unpredictable physical environments. AI may assist with monitoring data, predictive maintenance, documentation, and planning, but the core physical maintenance and repair tasks remain difficult to automate.

title: 3151. Ships' engineers (Level 5)
rationale: The work of a ship's engineer is primarily physical, involving the maintenance, operation, and repair of complex mechanical and electrical systems on board a vessel. While AI may assist in predictive maintenance and monitoring diagnostics, the core tasks require physical presence, manual dexterity, and real-time intervention in a harsh, unpredictable maritime environment.

title: 3152 Ships' deck officers and pilots (Level 4)
rationale: Ships' deck officers and pilots work primarily on physical vessels, navigating in real time, supervising crew, handling cargo and safety, and performing pilotage in confined waters. AI can assist with route planning, weather analysis, and documentation, and autonomous navigation may reshape parts of the role, but core responsibilities require physical presence and real-world judgment at sea.

title: 31521 Large ships' officers and mates (Level 5)
rationale: The role involves significant physical presence, real-time navigation, and safety-critical decision-making in unpredictable maritime environments. While AI and automation assist with navigation and monitoring systems, the core responsibilities require human oversight, physical intervention, and complex interpersonal coordination that remain largely outside the scope of current AI capabilities.

title: 3152. (Not more specifically classified) Ships' deck officers and pilots (Level 5)
rationale: The role involves significant physical presence, real-time navigation, and safety-critical decision-making in unpredictable maritime environments. While AI can assist with route optimization and automated monitoring systems, the core responsibilities require human oversight and physical intervention that remain largely outside the scope of current AI automation.

title: 31522 Small ships' officers (Level 5)
rationale: The role of a small ship's officer is primarily physical and operational, requiring real-time navigation, safety management, and manual control of a vessel in unpredictable maritime environments. While AI may assist with navigation systems and route optimization, the core responsibilities involving physical presence, emergency response, and hands-on vessel operation remain largely shielded from automation.

title: 31523 Harbour traffic controllers and harbour masters (Level 5)
rationale: While the role involves significant digital monitoring and information processing, it is tied to the physical coordination of maritime traffic and safety, which requires real-time human judgment and accountability. AI can assist with logistics and predictive modeling, but the high-stakes, unpredictable nature of physical harbour operations necessitates human oversight.

title: 3153 Aircraft pilots and related associate professionals (Level 4)
rationale: Aircraft piloting centers on real-time physical control of aircraft in unpredictable environments, with human presence legally required in the cockpit, which creates a strong natural barrier to AI. However, substantial parts of the job involve information processing such as flight planning, weather analysis, navigation, documentation, and communication, where AI tools can meaningfully assist. Automation of cockpit systems and potential future autonomy add some exposure, but the core work remains physical and safety-critical.

title: 3154 Air traffic controllers (Level 4)
rationale: Air traffic controllers work in real-time, safety-critical environments where they issue clearances, monitor radar and communicate directly with pilots, which keeps much of the core job tied to human presence and accountability. AI can meaningfully assist with information processing such as traffic flow forecasting, conflict detection alerts, and automated voice transcription, but regulatory requirements and the high cost of errors limit near-term displacement.

title: 3153. Aircraft pilots and related associate professionals (Level 5)
rationale: While flight systems are highly automated, the role requires critical physical presence, real-time decision-making in unpredictable environments, and ultimate responsibility for passenger safety. AI assists with navigation and monitoring, but the core requirement for human intervention in emergencies and complex physical operation keeps exposure low.

title: 3154. Air traffic controllers (Level 5)
rationale: While air traffic control involves significant information processing and monitoring, the role requires high-stakes, real-time decision-making and accountability that currently necessitates human oversight. AI is increasingly used for decision support and traffic optimization, but the physical safety requirements and the need for human intervention in unpredictable scenarios limit the extent of automation.

title: 3155. Air traffic safety electronics technicians (Level 5)
rationale: This role involves specialized technical maintenance of physical electronic systems, which requires on-site presence and manual intervention. While AI can assist in predictive maintenance and diagnostic data analysis, the critical nature of aviation safety necessitates human oversight and physical hardware interaction that limits automation potential.

title: 3155 Air traffic safety electronics technicians (Level 4)
rationale: Air traffic safety electronics technicians install, maintain, and repair physical navigation, radar, and communication equipment at airports and air traffic control facilities, work that requires hands-on presence and troubleshooting of hardware. AI may assist with diagnostics, predictive maintenance, and documentation, but the core physical repair and on-site equipment work remains largely unaffected.

title: 32 Health associate professionals (Level 2)
rationale: Health associate professionals perform tasks that require significant physical presence, clinical observation, and direct patient interaction, which limits the scope for full automation. While AI can assist with diagnostic support, documentation, and administrative efficiency, the core of the role remains rooted in human-centric care and physical assessment.

title: 3211 Medical imaging and therapeutic equipment technicians (Level 4)
rationale: Medical imaging and therapeutic equipment technicians spend much of their time operating, calibrating, and maintaining physical machines and positioning patients, which requires hands-on skill and in-person presence. AI can assist with image preprocessing, scheduling, and equipment diagnostics, but the core physical operation of the equipment and patient interaction remain largely human-driven.

title: 3211. Medical imaging and therapeutic equipment technicians (Level 5)
rationale: This role involves a significant physical component in operating specialized medical equipment and interacting with patients, which limits full automation. However, AI is rapidly advancing in image analysis and diagnostic support, which will significantly reshape the analytical portion of the technician's workflow.

title: 3212 Medical and pathology laboratory technicians (Level 4)
rationale: Medical and pathology laboratory technicians perform a mix of hands-on laboratory work, such as sample handling, pipetting, microscopy, and operating analyzers, which requires physical presence and manual skill. AI can meaningfully assist with result interpretation, quality control, data management, and automated image analysis, which are substantial information-processing parts of the role.

title: 321 Medical and pharmaceutical technicians (Level 3)
rationale: Medical and pharmaceutical technicians perform tasks that require significant physical presence, manual dexterity, and adherence to strict safety protocols in clinical or laboratory settings. While AI can assist with data analysis, diagnostic imaging interpretation, and inventory management, the core of the role remains tied to physical interaction with patients, samples, and equipment.

title: 3212. Medical and pathology laboratory technicians (Level 5)
rationale: The role involves a mix of physical laboratory tasks, such as sample preparation and equipment maintenance, and digital data processing. While AI is increasingly capable of automating diagnostic analysis and data entry, the physical handling of biological specimens and the requirement for human oversight in clinical settings provide a significant barrier to full automation.

title: 3213. Pharmaceutical technicians and assistants (Level 5)
rationale: Pharmaceutical technicians perform a mix of routine digital tasks, such as inventory management and prescription processing, and physical tasks like medication preparation and patient interaction. While AI can automate administrative and data-heavy workflows, the requirement for physical accuracy, safety oversight, and in-person patient counseling provides a significant barrier to full automation.

title: 3213 Pharmaceutical technicians and assistants (Level 4)
rationale: Pharmaceutical technicians and assistants do a mix of information-processing work, such as prescription records, inventory management, labeling, and documentation, which AI can meaningfully assist with. However, a substantial share of the job involves hands-on preparation of medicines, compounding, and physical handling of products in pharmacy or laboratory settings, which keeps exposure moderate.

title: 3214 Medical and dental prosthetic technicians (Level 4)
rationale: Medical and dental prosthetic technicians design, fabricate, and fit prostheses, orthoses, and dental appliances, which requires substantial hands-on manual skill and direct patient measurement and fitting. AI can assist with the digital design work such as CAD modeling, scan processing, and planning documentation, but the physical fabrication and in-person fitting remain a large share of the job.

title: 322 Nursing and midwifery associate professionals (Level 3)
rationale: This role involves significant physical, hands-on patient care and real-time clinical judgment that cannot be automated. While AI can assist with administrative tasks, documentation, and diagnostic support, the core requirement for human presence and physical interaction provides a strong barrier to full automation.

title: 32142 Prosthetist-orthotists (Level 5)
rationale: This occupation requires significant physical interaction, manual craftsmanship, and personalized fitting of medical devices for patients. While AI may assist in 3D modeling or design optimization, the core of the work remains hands-on, patient-centered, and dependent on physical assessment and manual fabrication skills.

title: 3221 Nursing associate professionals (Level 4)
rationale: Nursing associate professionals (ISCO 3221) perform mainly hands-on patient care, including medication administration, wound care, hygiene assistance, and monitoring vital signs, all requiring physical presence and real-time interaction with patients. AI can assist with peripheral tasks such as charting, documentation, scheduling, and clinical decision-support alerts, but the core bedside work remains largely untouched.

title: 32141 Dental technicians (Level 5)
rationale: Dental technicians perform highly skilled manual and technical work in a laboratory setting, which requires physical dexterity and precision that AI cannot currently replicate. While AI-driven CAD/CAM software and 3D printing are increasingly used to design and manufacture dental prosthetics, the role still requires significant human oversight, material handling, and physical craftsmanship.

title: 32211 Nurses (Level 5)
rationale: Nursing is a profession that requires significant physical presence, manual dexterity, and complex interpersonal interaction with patients. While AI can assist with administrative tasks, data analysis, and diagnostic support, the core of the job—providing physical care and emotional support—remains highly resistant to automation.

title: 3221. (Not more specifically classified) Nursing associate professionals (Level 5)
rationale: Nursing associate professionals perform tasks that require significant physical presence, manual dexterity, and real-time human interaction in unpredictable clinical environments. While AI can assist with administrative documentation and data analysis, the core of the role involves direct patient care that cannot be automated.

title: 32212 Public health nurses (Level 5)
rationale: Public health nursing involves significant physical presence, hands-on patient care, and complex interpersonal interaction that cannot be automated. While AI can assist with administrative tasks, documentation, and data analysis, the core of the profession requires human judgment and physical engagement.

title: 3222. Midwifery associate professionals (Level 5)
rationale: Midwifery associate professionals perform highly physical, hands-on clinical work that requires real-time human presence and complex interpersonal interaction. While AI may assist with administrative tasks or diagnostic data analysis, the core of the role—providing physical care and support during childbirth—remains largely shielded from automation.

title: 3222 Midwifery associate professionals (Level 4)
rationale: Midwifery work is centered on hands-on physical care, in-person monitoring of mothers and newborns, delivery assistance, and emotionally sensitive real-time interaction that AI cannot perform. AI may assist with documentation, scheduling, and clinical record-keeping or decision support, but these are peripheral to the core role.

title: 323 Traditional and complementary medicine associate professionals (Level 3)
rationale: This occupation involves hands-on, physical, and interpersonal interaction with patients, which creates a significant barrier to AI automation. While AI may assist with administrative tasks or provide supplementary information, the core of the work requires physical presence and human-centric care.

title: 3230 Traditional and complementary medicine associate professionals (Level 4)
rationale: Traditional and complementary medicine practitioners such as acupuncturists, herbalists, and massage or manual therapists perform hands-on, physically present treatments and rely heavily on in-person patient interaction and touch. AI could assist with peripheral tasks like appointment scheduling, record keeping, and information lookup, but it does not substantially touch the core therapeutic work.

title: 324 Veterinary technicians and assistants (Level 3)
rationale: Veterinary technicians perform essential physical and hands-on tasks, such as animal handling, administering treatments, and assisting in surgeries, which are difficult to automate. While AI can assist with administrative tasks, diagnostic imaging analysis, and record-keeping, the core of the job requires physical presence and real-time interaction with animals.

title: 3240 Veterinary technicians and assistants (Level 4)
rationale: Veterinary technicians and assistants spend most of their time on hands-on physical work such as restraining and handling animals, taking samples, preparing and administering treatments, and nursing patients, all of which require physical presence and real-time interaction. AI can help with peripheral tasks like record keeping, appointment scheduling, inventory, and summarizing clinical notes, but it does not touch the core animal-care work.

title: 3230. Traditional and complementary medicine associate professionals (Level 5)
rationale: This occupation relies heavily on physical, hands-on techniques and direct, in-person interaction with patients, which creates a significant barrier to AI automation. While AI may assist with administrative tasks like scheduling or record-keeping, the core therapeutic work requires human presence and physical touch.

title: 325 Other health associate professionals (Level 3)
rationale: This category includes diverse health associate professionals who primarily perform physical, patient-facing tasks that require human presence and clinical judgment. While AI can assist with administrative documentation and diagnostic data analysis, the core of the work remains rooted in physical interaction and real-time care delivery.

title: 3240. Veterinary technicians and assistants (Level 5)
rationale: Veterinary technicians perform essential physical tasks such as animal handling, clinical procedures, and laboratory work that cannot be automated. While AI can assist with administrative tasks, scheduling, and diagnostic image analysis, the core of the role requires physical presence and human-animal interaction.

title: 3251 Dental assistants and therapists (Level 4)
rationale: Dental assistants and therapists work mainly with patients in person, performing hands-on procedures such as assisting during treatment, preparing instruments, and providing oral care in a clinical setting. AI may help with peripheral tasks like scheduling, charting, and record-keeping, and AI-assisted imaging may affect some diagnostic support, but the core physical, interpersonal work remains largely untouched.

title: 3251. Dental assistants and therapists (Level 5)
rationale: The role is primarily physical and requires real-time, hands-on interaction with patients in a clinical setting, which creates a high barrier to automation. While AI may assist with administrative tasks like scheduling or record-keeping, the core clinical duties remain fundamentally human-centric.

title: 3255 Physiotherapy technicians and assistants (Level 4)
rationale: Physiotherapy technicians and assistants carry out hands-on treatment, exercise guidance, and patient handling that require physical presence and manual skill, which AI cannot perform. AI may assist with peripheral tasks such as documentation, scheduling, and patient education materials, but these make up a small share of the core work.

title: 3254. Dispensing opticians (Level 5)
rationale: The role involves a significant amount of physical, face-to-face interaction with customers for fitting and adjusting eyewear, which provides a natural barrier to automation. While AI can assist with administrative tasks, inventory management, and potentially optimizing lens measurements, the core requirement for physical presence and interpersonal service remains essential.

title: 3254 Dispensing opticians (Level 4)
rationale: Dispensing opticians combine knowledge work (prescription interpretation, lens specifications, inventory and order management, customer records) with substantial hands-on and face-to-face work such as fitting frames, adjusting eyewear, and advising customers in store. AI can meaningfully assist with the administrative and product-selection parts, and virtual try-on and automated measurement tools are advancing, but the in-person fitting and customer interaction keep the core job largely physical and interpersonal.

title: 3255. Physiotherapy technicians and assistants (Level 5)
rationale: Physiotherapy assistants perform tasks that are primarily physical, requiring direct manual interaction with patients and real-time monitoring of physical movements. While AI can assist with administrative scheduling or documentation, it cannot replace the core requirement of hands-on physical therapy and human presence.

title: 3257 Environmental and occupational health inspectors and associates (Level 4)
rationale: This work mixes on-site physical inspections, measurements, and face-to-face interactions with workplaces, facilities, and staff with substantial desk-based knowledge work such as reviewing documentation, writing inspection reports, interpreting regulations, and tracking compliance. AI can meaningfully assist with report drafting, data analysis, and regulatory research, but the field inspection and human judgment components keep the core job from being fully digital.

title: 3258 Ambulance workers (Level 4)
rationale: Ambulance work is centered on hands-on patient care, driving, lifting and stabilizing patients, and making real-time decisions in unpredictable physical environments at emergency scenes. AI may assist with documentation, dispatch support, or clinical decision aids, but the core job requires physical presence and manual skill, keeping exposure low.

title: 3257. Environmental and occupational health inspectors and associates (Level 5)
rationale: This role involves a mix of physical site inspections and data-driven reporting, requiring human judgment and on-site presence that AI cannot currently replicate. While AI can significantly streamline the documentation, data analysis, and regulatory compliance aspects of the job, the core requirement for physical verification and interpersonal enforcement remains.

title: 3258. Ambulance workers (Level 5)
rationale: Ambulance work is primarily physical, requiring real-time human intervention, manual skills, and complex decision-making in unpredictable, high-stakes environments. While AI may assist with administrative tasks or diagnostic support, the core of the role—providing emergency medical care and patient transport—remains inherently human-centric.

title: 3259 Health associate professionals not elsewhere classified (Level 4)
rationale: ISCO 3259 covers health associate professionals not elsewhere classified, such as various therapy and clinical support roles that combine hands-on patient care with documentation and information processing. AI can meaningfully assist with records, scheduling, and diagnostic information handling, but a substantial share of the work requires physical presence and direct patient interaction, placing it in the moderate range.

title: 3259. (Not more specifically classified) Health associate professionals not elsewhere classified (Level 5)
rationale: This category covers a diverse range of health support roles that typically require physical presence, patient interaction, and manual tasks. While AI can assist with administrative documentation and data processing, the core of the work relies on human-centric care and physical intervention that remains resistant to automation.

title: 32591 Occupational therapists (Level 5)
rationale: Occupational therapy requires significant physical interaction, manual dexterity, and real-time human empathy to assess and treat patients. While AI can assist with administrative tasks, documentation, and suggesting treatment plans, the core of the work relies on physical presence and personalized human care that cannot be automated.

title: 32592 Other therapists (Level 5)
rationale: This role involves specialized, hands-on therapeutic interventions that require physical presence and nuanced human interaction. While AI may assist with administrative tasks or documentation, the core of the work relies on direct, real-time physical and emotional engagement with patients, which is highly resistant to automation.

title: 331 Financial and mathematical associate professionals (Level 3)
rationale: This occupation involves highly structured, digital tasks such as data analysis, financial reporting, and mathematical modeling, which are primary targets for AI automation. Because the work is almost entirely computer-based and relies on processing information, AI tools can already perform or significantly accelerate the majority of core functions.

title: 33 Business and administration associate professionals (Level 2)
rationale: This occupation consists primarily of digital knowledge work, including administrative support, data processing, and business coordination tasks that are highly susceptible to automation. AI tools are already capable of handling significant portions of these workflows, leading to a high likelihood of major restructuring in how these roles are performed.

title: 3311 Securities and finance dealers and brokers (Level 4)
rationale: Securities and finance dealers and brokers work almost entirely on computers, handling trade execution, market analysis, client communication, and compliance documentation, all digital tasks where AI is advancing quickly. Algorithmic trading and AI-driven analytics already automate much of the routine work, while human relationship management, client trust, and regulatory accountability keep some judgment-based and interpersonal core in place.

title: 3311. Securities and finance dealers and brokers (Level 5)
rationale: This role is almost entirely digital, involving the analysis of financial data, market monitoring, and the execution of trades via computer systems. AI is already highly capable of processing market information, identifying trends, and automating execution, which significantly restructures the core functions of this occupation.

title: 3312 Credit and loans officers (Level 4)
rationale: Credit and loan officers work primarily with financial documents, applications, data analysis, and risk models, all of which are digital and highly amenable to AI automation such as automated underwriting and document processing. Some human judgment, customer relationship management, and in-person meetings remain, which keeps the score below the very highest levels.

title: 3312. Credit and loans officers (Level 5)
rationale: Credit and loan officer tasks are primarily digital, involving data analysis, risk assessment, and document processing, all of which are core domains for AI advancement. While human judgment is required for final approvals and client relationships, the analytical and administrative components are highly susceptible to automation and AI-driven decision support.

title: 3313. Accounting associate professionals (Level 5)
rationale: Accounting associate professional tasks are primarily digital, involving data entry, reconciliation, and financial reporting, which are highly susceptible to automation by AI and specialized accounting software. Because the core work is performed entirely on a computer with structured data, AI tools can already handle a significant portion of these routine analytical and administrative functions.

title: 3313 Accounting associate professionals (Level 4)
rationale: Accounting associate professionals work almost entirely on a computer, processing bookkeeping entries, reconciling accounts, preparing financial statements and tax forms, and checking invoices. These are structured, rule-based digital tasks in which AI is improving rapidly and can automate much of the routine processing.
